page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured within the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on a shared CPU allocation model and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.mn4.8xlarge demonstrates average multi-core processing capabilities, as evidenced by its mid-tier scores in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with both stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression, perform poorly, ranking in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks like bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang achieve average performance tiers.

The memory subsystem exhibits average read and write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the lower 25%. For application workloads, the instance delivers average throughput in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and database operations. Large language model inference speeds for prompt processing and text generation using small and medium models also align with average performance tiers, though text generation on smaller models is relatively weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and balanced resource distribution, the ecs.mn4.8xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning or high single-core performance. It is suited for general-purpose applications, multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, and moderate database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz on a shared CPU allocation. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff: while multi-core performance, software compilation, and static web serving reach average tiers, single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression are weak. The memory subsystem provides average read and write bandwidth, though overall memory scores skew lower. This resource profile makes the instance a qualitatively cost-effective option for multi-threaded workloads, moderate database operations, and general-purpose web serving where dedicated CPU execution is not strictly required.
